task_template.title: Tell the IRS your new address
task_template.description: The IRS mails notices and refunds to the address it has on file. Form 8822 updates your home mailing address.
steps: Download Form 8822 from IRS.gov.
Fill in your old and new address.
Mail it to the IRS address listed in the form instructions for your old state.

financial.note: A missed IRS notice can turn into late-payment interest.

task_template.title: Review your quarterly estimated tax payments
task_template.description: With 1099 or self-employment income, no employer withholds tax for you. The IRS says you generally have to make estimated payments if you expect to owe $1,000 or more when you file.
steps: Estimate this year's income and tax with the Form 1040-ES worksheet.
Pay each quarter through IRS Direct Pay or your IRS online account.
Check whether {destination} also expects state estimated payments.

deadline.label: Quarterly: April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15 (next business day if the date falls on a weekend or holiday)

financial.note: Underpaying a quarter can add an IRS underpayment penalty.

task_template.title: Plan for a California part-year resident return
task_template.description: If you move into California during the year, the Franchise Tax Board treats you as a part-year resident. Part-year residents who meet the income thresholds file Form 540NR.
steps: Write down the exact date you became a California resident.
Keep pay records split by before and after the move.
At tax time, file Form 540NR with Schedule CA (540NR).
documents: W-2s and 1099s for the full year

deadline.label: Filed with your state return for the year of the move

financial.note: California taxes all income received while you are a resident.

source_name: California FTB — Part-year resident and nonresident

task_template.title: Give your employer a California DE 4
task_template.description: The federal W-4 only covers federal withholding. California income tax withholding is set by the state DE 4. Without a valid DE 4, an employer withholds as single with zero allowances.
steps: Download the DE 4 from the EDD site.
Complete it with your filing status and allowances.
Hand it to your employer's payroll team together with your new address.

financial.note: Wrong state withholding shows up as a bill or an oversized refund at tax time.

task_template.title: Check whether {origin} expects a final state return
task_template.description: States that tax income usually want a part-year return for the months you lived there. Civio has not verified the rule for {origin}.
steps: Open the {origin} tax agency site from the official directory.
Look for part-year resident filing rules.
Note the form name and due date in this task.

financial.note: Income earned before the move may be taxable in {origin}.

task_template.title: Check {destination} income tax and withholding rules
task_template.description: Your new state may tax income and need its own withholding form. Civio has not verified the rule for {destination}.
steps: Open the {destination} tax agency site from the official directory.
Check whether the state taxes wages and which withholding form employers use.
Look for part-year resident filing rules.
documents: Your first pay stub after the move

financial.note: State withholding may start, stop or change with the move.

task_template.title: Enroll through Covered California
task_template.description: A Marketplace plan from another state does not follow you. Moving to California is a qualifying life event, and Covered California generally gives you 60 days from the move date to apply.
steps: Start a new application at CoveredCA.com with your California address.
Compare plans available in your new ZIP code.
Pick a plan, then end your old-state plan so the coverage dates line up.
documents: Proof of your new address and move date (lease, utility bill)
Social Security numbers for everyone applying

deadline.label: Generally 60 days from the date of your move

financial.note: Miss the window and you wait for the next open enrollment without a plan.

task_template.title: Review Marketplace coverage for {destination}
task_template.description: When you move to a new state you need a new Marketplace application. The move qualifies you for a Special Enrollment Period: in most cases you have 60 days from your move date to enroll.
steps: Start a new application for {destination} at HealthCare.gov (it redirects you if the state runs its own exchange).
Compare plans for your new ZIP code.
Pick a plan, then end the old plan so the coverage dates line up.
documents: Proof of your new address and move date
Proof you had coverage for at least 1 day in the 60 days before the move, if asked

deadline.label: In most cases, 60 days from your move date

financial.note: Miss the window and you wait for the next open enrollment without a plan.

source_name: HealthCare.gov — What if you move out of state

task_template.title: Apply for Medicaid in {destination}
task_template.description: Medicaid is run state by state and you generally must be a resident of the state that covers you. Coverage from {origin} does not transfer: apply in {destination} and report the move to {origin}.
steps: Apply with the {destination} Medicaid agency using the address where you intend to live.
Report your change of residency to the {origin} Medicaid agency.
Keep both notices until the new coverage is confirmed.

financial.note: A gap between the two states means paying for care out of pocket.

task_template.title: Ask HR whether your plan works in {destination}
task_template.description: Employer plans differ on out-of-area coverage. Civio found no official rule that covers every plan, so this one is yours to confirm with your benefits team.
steps: Ask HR whether your plan's network covers {destination}.
Ask whether the move lets you change plans outside open enrollment.
Update your home address in the benefits system.
documents: Your plan's Summary of Benefits and Coverage

financial.note: Out-of-network care is usually billed at a higher rate.

source_name: U.S. Department of Labor — Employee Benefits Security Administration

task_template.title: Register your vehicle in California
task_template.description: The California DMV requires a vehicle from another state to be registered within 20 days of establishing residency or accepting employment in California. The DMV advises submitting the application and fees on time even if some paperwork is still missing.
steps: Get a smog certification from a California smog station, if your vehicle needs one.
Complete form REG 343, signed by every registered owner.
Bring the vehicle to a DMV office for VIN verification (REG 31). An appointment is recommended.
Hand in the out-of-state title, registration and plates, and pay the fees.

deadline.label: Within 20 days of establishing residency or accepting employment in California

financial.note: Registration fees and use tax are due. Late registration adds DMV penalties.

source_name: California DMV — New California resident portal

task_template.title: Collect proof of your California address
task_template.description: The DMV asks for documents that show you live in California when you apply for a driver license. Without them the office visit does not count, so this comes before the license.
steps: Open the DMV's list of accepted residency documents.
Pick documents that show your name and new California address, such as a signed lease or a utility bill.
Keep the originals together with your identity document for the DMV visit.
documents: California residency documents from the DMV's accepted list
Identity document from the DMV's accepted list

source_name: California DMV — Requirements for a California driver's license

task_template.title: Get a California driver license
task_template.description: If you become a California resident and drive, the DMV says you must get a California driver license within 10 days.
steps: Start the driver license application on the DMV site.
Book a DMV office visit.
Bring your identity and residency documents and your current license.
documents: Identity and California residency documents listed by the DMV

deadline.label: Within 10 days of becoming a California resident

financial.note: The DMV charges an application fee.

source_name: California DMV — Requirements for a California driver's license

task_template.title: Move your auto insurance to a California policy
task_template.description: California's minimum liability limits rose on January 1, 2025: $30,000 for injury or death of one person, $60,000 per accident, and $15,000 for property damage.
steps: Tell your insurer your move date and California garaging address.
Confirm the new policy meets the 30/60/15 minimum.
Keep proof of insurance for your DMV registration visit.

financial.note: Your premium is re-rated for the new address.

source_name: California Department of Insurance — Automobile insurance guide

task_template.title: Register your vehicle in Texas
task_template.description: The Texas DMV gives new residents 30 days from the move to register a vehicle in the state.
steps: Get Texas auto insurance.
Complete Form 130-U (Application for Texas Title and/or Registration).
Take the paperwork to your county tax assessor-collector office.

deadline.label: Within 30 days of moving to Texas

financial.note: Registration fees are due. Registering late may add penalty fees.

task_template.title: Get a Texas driver license
task_template.description: New residents are required to get a Texas driver license from the Department of Public Safety within 90 days of moving to the state.
steps: Book an appointment with a DPS driver license office.
Bring proof of identity and Texas residency.
Surrender your out-of-state license.

deadline.label: Within 90 days of moving to Texas

financial.note: DPS charges a license fee.

task_template.title: Check which {destination} DMV deadlines apply to you
task_template.description: Every state sets its own deadline for new residents to register a vehicle and swap their license. Civio has not verified the rule for {destination}.
steps: Open the {destination} motor vehicle agency from the official directory.
Check licensing if you will drive and registration if you are bringing a vehicle.
List the documents the agency asks for.

financial.note: States commonly charge late fees for missed registration deadlines.

task_template.title: Move your auto insurance to a Florida policy
task_template.description: Florida requires a vehicle registered in the state to carry at least $10,000 of property damage liability, and no-fault (PIP) security under the Motor Vehicle No-Fault Law.
steps: Tell your insurer your move date and Florida garaging address.
Confirm the policy has property damage liability of at least $10,000 and the no-fault coverage Florida requires.
Keep proof of insurance for your registration visit.

financial.note: Your premium is re-rated for the new address.

task_template.title: Register your vehicle in Florida
task_template.description: A nonresident who takes a job or enrolls children in a Florida public school must register motor vehicles in Florida within 10 days after the job or schooling begins.
steps: Get a Florida auto insurance policy first.
Complete the Florida title and registration application for an out-of-state vehicle.
Take the paperwork, VIN verification and your old title to a county tax collector office.

deadline.label: Within 10 days of starting work or enrolling children in school in Florida

financial.note: Registration fees are due. Late registration can add penalties.

task_template.title: Get a Florida driver license
task_template.description: A nonresident who takes a job or enrolls children in a Florida public school must get a Florida driver license within 30 days if they drive in the state. Their spouse and dependent children are covered by the same 30-day rule.
steps: Book an appointment at a driver license office or tax collector office.
Bring identity, Social Security and Florida residency documents.
Surrender your out-of-state license.
documents: Two proofs of Florida residential address

deadline.label: Within 30 days of starting work or enrolling children in school in Florida

financial.note: A license fee is charged.

task_template.title: Move your auto insurance to a Washington policy
task_template.description: Washington requires drivers to be able to show financial responsibility for their vehicle, and a driver cited without it can be fined.
steps: Tell your insurer your move date and Washington garaging address.
Ask the insurer for a card or proof of coverage that you can carry in the vehicle.
Keep proof of insurance for your registration visit.

financial.note: Your premium is re-rated for the new address.

task_template.title: Register your vehicle in Washington
task_template.description: New Washington residents must register their vehicles within thirty days of becoming residents. Becoming a registered voter or declaring residency to get a state license counts as evidence of residency.
steps: Get Washington auto insurance.
Apply through a county auditor or vehicle licensing office with your out-of-state title and registration.
Pay the registration fees and surrender your old plates if asked.

deadline.label: Within 30 days of becoming a Washington resident

financial.note: Fees are due. Late registration can add penalties.

task_template.title: Get a Washington driver license
task_template.description: New Washington residents must get a Washington driver license within thirty days of becoming residents, and must surrender any licenses issued by another jurisdiction.
steps: Start the application with the Washington Department of Licensing.
Visit a licensing office with your identity and residency documents.
Surrender your out-of-state license.

deadline.label: Within 30 days of becoming a Washington resident

financial.note: A license fee is charged.

task_template.title: Register your vehicle in New York
task_template.description: The New York DMV requires you to register a vehicle here within 30 days of becoming a resident. Registration needs proof of ownership, insurance and that sales taxes were paid. Keep your old insurance in place until the new registration is done.
steps: Get New York auto insurance.
Complete the Vehicle Registration/Title Application (MV-82).
Bring proof of ownership, insurance and identity to a DMV office.

deadline.label: Within 30 days of becoming a New York resident

financial.note: Registration fees and sales tax are due. An unregistered vehicle can lead to suspension.

source_name: New York DMV — Register an out-of-state vehicle

task_template.title: Get a New York driver license
task_template.description: If you become a New York resident, the DMV says you must get a New York driver license within 30 days.
steps: Check what documents the DMV needs for your situation.
Visit a DMV office with proof of name, date of birth and Social Security.
Turn in your out-of-state license and pass the vision test.
documents: Proof of identity and date of birth

deadline.label: Within 30 days of becoming a New York resident

financial.note: The DMV charges a license fee.

source_name: New York DMV — Driving in New York State

task_template.title: Plan for a New York part-year resident return
task_template.description: If you move into New York during the tax year, the Tax Department says you file Form IT-203, the nonresident and part-year resident return.
steps: Write down the exact date you became a New York resident.
Keep pay records split by before and after the move.
At tax time, file Form IT-203 for the year of the move.
documents: W-2s and 1099s for the full year

deadline.label: Filed with your state return for the year of the move

financial.note: New York taxes income you receive as a New York resident, and New York-source income before.

source_name: New York Tax Department — IT-203 information

task_template.title: Enroll your child in a California school
task_template.description: In California, children between 6 and 18 are subject to compulsory full-time education. A child is admitted to kindergarten if they turn five on or before September 1 of the school year.
steps: Find the school district for your new address.
Ask the district for its enrollment document list.
Bring your child's immunization record to registration.
Request records from the previous school.
documents: Immunization record (checked at admission under California Department of Public Health rules)
Other documents on your school district's enrollment list

deadline.label: Before your child's first school day after the move

source_name: California Department of Education — Kindergarten FAQ

task_template.title: Check school enrollment requirements in {destination}
task_template.description: School age cut-offs, immunization rules and enrollment documents are set by each state and district. Civio has not verified the rule for {destination}.
steps: Find the school district for your new address.
Ask for its enrollment document list and immunization requirements.
Request records from the previous school.

source_name: U.S. Department of Education — State contacts
